says: Mulled ale, hot as you like. Sit by the fire, thaw your fingers.
The whole village fits in here at midwinter. Smells like it too.
Shall I sing of the tower that tumbled? Seven verses. Eight if the ale holds.
Every song up here ends with someone frozen solid. It's tradition.
Every log I split now is one less shiver come midwinter.
Mind the pines when the wind's up. They drop their snow on your head and laugh about it.
White since I was twenty. The cold gets into your hair up here, they say.
Sven's my brother. He chops, I chop. Nobody in Tumbledown ever died of too much firewood.
Cut the hole, drop the line, wait. Then wait. Then go home cold.
The ice is thick this close in. Out past the edge it's black water all the way to Ravenford.
Sixty winters on this ice. It's never let me through yet. Touch wood.
When the lights burn green over Nightspire, the fish go deep. They know.
Grandad Haldor says talk quietly on the ice. The fish listen.
Three herring and a boot. The boot's mine, I'm keeping it.
Clear the road at dawn, it's snowed under by noon. Clear it again. That's the job.
Came up the coast road, did you? It's the only way in that the snow doesn't close.

folk.says: Path to the well, path to the shore, path to the longhall. Mostly the longhall.
Pine cones burn hot and quick. I fill a basket a day and we're still short.

says: The ice tears nets like paper. So I mend, and Astrid tears them again.
Haldor's my father. Don't let him tell you about the whale.
Boats wait for the thaw. I don't. A line through the ice catches the same fish.
Herring for the smokehouse, cod for the pot, and the odd trout when the gods are kind.
Fox and hare this winter. Wolves in the deep wood, but I leave them be.
West through the pines there's a hole in the hill they call Shadowmaw. My dogs won't go near it.
